response.summary: The component structure, copy, reading order, tests and docs match the plan. Two defects remain. First, the "cool-neutral" colors were verified only in a dev fixture that omits `activity-centre.css`. In the app, that file re-pins the same semantic variables to warm cream, so the page will still be beige and warm-bordered. Second, `supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts` is in the change manifest. It is generated dirt containing a machine-local absolute import path, and the plan says it must stay uncommitted. I did not run tests or view the screenshots.

findings.evidence: The CSS builds its grounds from `hsl(var(--background))`, `--card`, `--border`, `--foreground` and `--primary`. `ActivityRunner.tsx:44` imports `activity-centre.css`, and `ActivityCentre.tsx:11` and `ActivityLab.tsx:122` import it too. That file pins `.activity-centre { --background: 38 36% 93%; --card: 40 50% 98%; --border: 36 20% 84%; --foreground: 30 17% 9%; --primary: 30 17% 12% }`. The `.activity-centre.act-home` wrapper therefore resolves to warm cream and tan hairlines with warm near-black ink. The plan requires cool-neutral page and white example grounds and rejects a beige look. The local fixture `src/dev/relationship-intro-preview.tsx` imports only `index.css` and `activities-home.css`. It never imports `activity-centre.css`. The recorded measurements (page `rgb(252,252,252)`, button `rgb(18,18,18)`) are the root light tokens, not what students will see. The before/after screenshots and the README claim of 'neutral' are likewise unrepresentative of production.
findings.fix: Scope the neutral tokens explicitly on `.relationship-intro`. For example, define `--relationship-page` and `--relationship-card` as cool neutral values, taken from the root Workroom light tokens (`0 0% 99%` and `0 0% 100%`) or the Workroom tokens that `index.css` already defines. Do the same for border, ink and primary. Also set the `.activity-centre.act-home[data-world="spot-the-relationship"]` background to the same value. Alternatively, import `activity-centre.css` in the preview fixture and re-measure in that condition. Then regenerate the screenshots, `layout-measurements.json` and the README claims, and run the contrast check on the real computed values.

findings.evidence: The file is in the change manifest and the tracked diff. It replaces about 590 bundled lines with `import mcp from "npm:C:\\Users\\Joshu\\dev\\ai-os-projects\\lsatu-relationship-ui\\src\\lib\\mcp\\index.ts"`, a machine-local absolute path that would break the edge function when deployed. The plan states this generated dirt must remain untouched and uncommitted.
findings.fix: Exclude it from the commit and the review bundle. Use `git add` on explicit paths only. Run `git restore` on it, or leave it unstaged, before using `safe-push.sh`. Confirm the final diff does not list it.

findings.evidence: The `video` background and the focus outline use `--relationship-ink`. If a dark theme ever applies, the ink is near-white, so the video letterbox is light. `.activity-centre` forces `color-scheme: light`, so this is mostly latent. The README reports a root-dark resume screenshot (`after-root-dark-resume.png`) taken from the fixture, which is not a production state.
findings.fix: Use a fixed dark value for the video backdrop. Label the root-dark screenshot as a fixture-only condition, or drop it.

findings.evidence: The `@media (max-width: 800px)` block repeats the `@container` block rule for rule. The layout is duplicated, so the two rule sets can drift apart.
findings.fix: Keep only the `@container` rule (supported in current evergreen browsers) or add a comment that the media query is a deliberate fallback. In `RelationshipIntro.tsx`, also fix the inconsistent indentation of the nested `relationship-written` block.

coverage: Read relationship-intro.css and the diffs of the tests, JSON, presentation constant, DESIGN.md and the surface brief.

Grepped src for the old rejected strings (Worked example, What to write, Teacher preview, Name each relationship). The remaining hits are unrelated activities, and the one hit in ActivityRunner is a comment.
Traced the CSS variables across `index.css` and `activity-centre.css`. Traced `activity-centre.css` importers.
Sampled `layout-measurements.json` and the README by grep.
limitations: I could not run tests, typecheck or build, and I make no claim that they pass.
I could not view the PNG screenshots, so the visual claims are unverified.
I did not read every README line or the whole `layout-measurements.json`; both were only grepped.
I did not check the vault documents (`COPY-CORRECTIONS`, the memory note) or the plan-dispositions file, because they are outside the repository checkout.
